title: "Lab · Hello Pico"

The lab for this lesson is the shared **Hello Pico** lab. It lives at
the repository root so it can be reused from other courses.

## The smallest supported Pico today

[`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §3 records that `labs/hello-pico`
is the smallest end-to-end path a learner can complete today without
installing Kubernetes, a message broker, a database, an AI library, or
a bot platform. Its only prerequisites are a shell, a text editor,
Python 3.8+ on `PATH`, and a local clone of this repository (which
ships `bin/pico`).

Use this lab to see the current Rules → Parser → Composer → Pico
pipeline run from one Rule file to one executable artefact, before
later lessons add any optional capability.

## Where to go

Open the [Hello Pico lab](../../../../labs/hello-pico/) and follow the
walkthrough. It uses the shared lab template with these pages:

- [Objectives](../../../../labs/hello-pico/objectives.html)
- [Walkthrough](../../../../labs/hello-pico/walkthrough.html)
- [Solution](../../../../labs/hello-pico/solution.html)

## What you will produce

By the end of the lab you will have a working `hello-world-pico` — the
`produces` entry from the course [metadata](../../metadata.yaml) — and
you will have exercised each stage of the pipeline named in the
[lesson](index.qmd): a Rule in YAML, `pico parse`, `pico compose`, and
one run of the composed artefact.

## What this lab does *not* do

This lab does not ask you to author a capsule file or an OE-shaped
Pico resource. The capsule contract shown in the lesson is the memo26
proposal and is not yet adopted upstream (see the lesson callout).
Composing capability capsules is a later concern that depends on an
upstream decision; this lab stays inside the dependency-free
Rules → Parser → Composer pipeline.
